newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Plessey wins Philippine traffic contract.
newsitem.headline: Plessey wins Philippine traffic contract.

text.p: South African electronics group Plessey Corp Ltd on Tuesday announced it had won a 100 million rand contract to modernise the traffic system in the Philippine capital, Manila.

"A 100 million rand contract to modernise the traffic system in the Philippines' capital of Manila has been won by the Plessey electronics group through its subsidiary, Plessey Asia Pacific," the company said in a statement.
Plessey Corp's chief executive John Temple said the contract was a further indication of expected earnings contributions from the group's electronics businesses in the Pacific Rim.
"The Manila business follows a 67 million rand digital radio equipment contract in the Philippines and a 10 million rand extension to a Hong Kong traffic systems contract.

"These and other potential contracts strengthen our view that the traffic, navigational systems and communications businesses we acquired from the Australian group AWA last January could lift offshore turnover to 30 percent of group sales in the current financial year," the group said.
Plessey's turnover in the year to end March 1997 was 1.3 billion rand. It paid 70 million rand for the AWA businesses, which form the core of Plessey Asia Pacific.
Temple said that Plessey was also pursuing opportunities in communications, broadcasting and other professional electronics in the Pacific Rim.
